title: Paper Presheaf · Local evidence, scoped synthesis
description: A curated finite presheaf over scoped paper facts, with literal restriction maps, cross-paper contract screens and a separate copresheaf of fixed artifact availability.

mathematics.base: Finite discrete variable space K; contexts are subsets U ⊆ K, with union covers and inclusion arrows. Five topic views group ports for reading; they do not define empirical equivalence.
mathematics.eventSheaf: E(U) = ∏_{k∈U} D_k. Restriction to V⊆U projects an assignment onto V. Compatible complete local assignments merge uniquely in E.
mathematics.presheaf: F(U) contains complete assignments in E(U) satisfying each declared constraint whose full support lies in U. Projection preserves those constraints, so F is a presheaf. Cross-patch constraints can obstruct existence of a glue.
mathematics.copresheaf: I(U) is the set of fixed evidence/contract-definition artifacts with support contained in U. U⊆V gives inclusion I(U)→I(V). This is availability, not artifact generation, empirical confirmation or a cosheaf claim.
mathematics.gluing: Check matching restrictions on overlaps; merge local assignments; then test the joint screen. A fully observed compatible local family can fail to give a section of F on its union. F is separated: uniqueness is inherited from assignments.
mathematics.unknown: null is an unobserved partial record, not a domain value or a mathematical section. Finite completions are hypothetical possibilities, never new evidence. An unresolved packet is not called a certified gluing counterexample.
mathematics.sheafification: For this discrete base, sheafification retains singleton stalk data and can discard cross-variable constraints. It is not a scientifically valid repair button.

limitations: Paper ports are curated, lossy scoped projections from the existing pinned readings, not an automatically learned ontology or a complete interpretation of each paper.

Restriction maps are literal projections and mathematically checked. Cross-paper material/causal translation maps are candidate interfaces, not verified morphisms; bounded passes describe scoped comparisons or inventories.
A passed Boolean screen verifies consistency of this encoding and contract. It does not validate causality, physical equivalence, universal novelty or an unperformed scientific experiment.
A blocked packet does not show the papers contradict or that every global section is impossible. It shows this selected packet cannot satisfy the chosen screen.
The stronger scope often deliberately requests an unsupported extrapolation. It is displayed to reveal missing interfaces, not to attribute that claim to the authors.
Withholding and overlap-conflict controls are synthetic demonstrations. They never edit source observations or constitute new experiments.
PROTOTYPE is abstract-only and FieldPerceiver partially read. Unknown interfaces remain null and may require reading before any scientific test.
All reader, auditor and coordinator contexts share one model family. No independent scientific reproduction or theorem-prover certification was performed.
No cohomology groups, sheaf Laplacians, learned restriction maps or statistically independent latent factors are computed.

papers.title: Nature designs tough collagen: Explaining the nanostructure of collagen fibrils

surprise.observation: Stronger adhesion can eventually favor brittle molecular rupture.
surprise.interpretation: Maximizing bond strength alone need not maximize toughness.
surprise.boundary: Model mechanics do not establish evolutionary optimization.

detail.observation: The slip threshold shifts from roughly 42 nm in pairs to 200 nm in fibrils.
detail.consequence: Boundary conditions and confinement change the inferred design scale.

papers.title: Nanoconfinement controls stiffness, strength and mechanical toughness of β-sheet crystals in silk
papers.version: Nature Materials 9, 359–367; published online March 14, 2010; author-hosted advance publication PDF

surprise.observation: Smaller crystals can simultaneously improve stiffness, strength and dissipation.
surprise.interpretation: Weak-bond architecture can overcome constituent weakness.
surprise.boundary: Nanocrystal behavior is not a complete model of whole silk.

detail.observation: Experimental-rate pull-out forces require an estimated sixfold reduction; the transition length survives rate variation.
detail.consequence: The robust claim concerns the mechanism and length scale, rather than raw simulated force.

papers.title: Category Theoretic Analysis of Hierarchical Protein Materials and Social Networks

surprise.observation: A slack connection can be functionally invisible until another connection fails.
surprise.interpretation: The useful abstraction includes conditional function, beyond connectivity.
surprise.boundary: The social example was deliberately designed to match the protein olog.

detail.observation: Figure 4 alone omits essential equalities and fiber-product definitions in Tables 1–2.
detail.consequence: A similar-looking graph is insufficient to establish the claimed correspondence.

papers.title: Categorical prototyping: incorporating molecular mechanisms into 3D printing

surprise.observation: The abstract reports examining a twisted physical prototype beyond the original model.
surprise.interpretation: A faithful partial embodiment may suggest additional questions.
surprise.boundary: This observation has not been checked against full results.

detail.observation: Only chosen mechanical properties are claimed to be retained.
detail.consequence: Geometric resemblance would not warrant assuming all nanoscale properties transfer.

papers.title: Self-Revising Discovery Systems for Science: A Categorical Framework for Agentic Artificial Intelligence

surprise.observation: Accepted law multiplies log-compliance by slow-mode participation.
surprise.interpretation: Local softness depends on collective participation.
surprise.boundary: An admitted product over existing GNM quantities; schema-relative novelty, not universal discovery.

detail.observation: V2 retains compliance; HEA fatigue replaces the main fiber-network case.
detail.consequence: Fiber AIC is supplementary; MDL gain is not categorical discovery cost.

papers.title: A Category-Theoretic Framework from Biological Mechanics to Engineered Stimulus-Response Systems

surprise.observation: Thermal twisting combines two previously tested modules.
surprise.interpretation: Validated interfaces can generate an additional actuator class.
surprise.boundary: Direct mechanics also derives it; one recombination demonstrates limited scope.

detail.observation: Validation measures equilibrium angles, n=3–4 per class.
detail.consequence: Transient accuracy and broad manufacturing robustness remain unestablished.

papers.title: Category Theory Based Solution for the Building Block Replacement Problem in Materials Design

surprise.observation: Seemingly distant mixtures share a replacement-query schema.
surprise.interpretation: Reusable relational structure can survive substrate changes.
surprise.boundary: Aggregation physics remains domain-specific; schema isomorphism does not equal physical equivalence.

detail.observation: Laminate calculation retains only in-plane ABD components.
detail.consequence: Out-of-plane replacement requires nonlinear solving and additional constraints.

papers.title: Materials by Design: Merging Proteins and Music

surprise.observation: Stronger individual proteins can fail to form fibers.
surprise.interpretation: Excessive local aggregation can defeat network formation.
surprise.boundary: Mechanism is reviewed prior experiment/simulation, not proof musical aesthetics predicts materials.

detail.observation: fMRI assessment and music-to-material improvement are future proposals.
detail.consequence: Performed sonification does not establish predictive reverse transfer.

papers.title: FieldPerceiver: Domain agnostic transformer model to predict multiscale physical fields and nonlinear material properties through neural ologs

surprise.interpretation: Attention learns effective relations without supplied constitutive properties.
surprise.boundary: Fixed A/B vocabulary is not autonomous schema revision.

surprise.boundary: One simulated alloy system does not establish universal design laws.

detail.consequence: Matching the descriptor does not recover the full dynamical operator.

bridges.label: Provenance through schema revision
bridges.scientificClaim: A distributed artifact chain could retain inspectable scientific meaning when its representation changes.

interfaceVariables.name: artifact_id
interfaceVariables.meaning: Immutable identity of a particular input or output artifact

interfaceVariables.name: schema_version
interfaceVariables.meaning: Explicit input and output vocabulary version

interfaceVariables.name: transport_witness
interfaceVariables.meaning: Declared map from a source-schema claim into a target-schema claim

requirements: Pin input artifacts, schema versions and interpretation before each revision.
Attach a typed transport witness and residual to each accepted change.
Check semantic meaning in addition to matching payload keys.
gaps: The reviewed ScienceClaw key-overlap rule alone does not verify semantic preservation.
COPRESHEAF formal conditions are not a certificate for the entire implemented artifact workflow.
bridges.canGlue: A versioned lineage record and a declared local claim-transport audit.
bridges.temptingOverreach: A common artifact key or provenance DAG proves that the revised scientific claim remains true.
bridges.boundedClaim: A typed comparison of declared schema revisions and artifact-needs coordination; no semantic-preserving runtime transport is certified.
bridges.strongerClaim: A common artifact key or provenance DAG proves that the revised scientific claim remains true.

bridges.label: Conditional function under structural transfer
bridges.scientificClaim: A chosen structure–function relation can be translated only under explicit interface and preservation conditions.

interfaceVariables.name: typed_relation
interfaceVariables.meaning: The chosen relation and its source/target types

interfaceVariables.name: composition_condition
interfaceVariables.meaning: Equalities, admissible queries or model-simulation conditions actually preserved

interfaceVariables.name: response_observable
interfaceVariables.meaning: The selected failure, elasticity or actuator response plus units and loading conditions

requirements: Name the specific source relation and intended target function.
Specify commuting equalities or simulation conditions for that chosen mapping.
Calibrate domain-specific physical laws and test the intended target observable.
gaps: Protein/social analogy is deliberately simplified.
Replacement example is in-plane; out-of-plane behavior needs extra solving.
STIMULUS validates equilibrium angles, not general time-dependent response.
bridges.canGlue: An interface contract for a selected relation and a bounded target observable.
bridges.temptingOverreach: A shared categorical schema proves physical equivalence or transfers every material property.
bridges.boundedClaim: A typed comparison of the papers’ separately declared preservation conditions; no actual composed cross-paper map is certified.
bridges.strongerClaim: A shared categorical schema proves physical equivalence or transfers every material property.

bridges.label: Modal capability without full dynamics
bridges.scientificClaim: Modal objectives can be made comparable only after specifying which part of the dynamics each workflow measures.

interfaceVariables.name: modal_descriptor
interfaceVariables.meaning: Amplitude profile, natural frequency or frequency-band density; never silently interchange these

interfaceVariables.name: mode_definition
interfaceVariables.meaning: Mode index, normalization, model and boundary conditions

interfaceVariables.name: system_realization
interfaceVariables.meaning: Protein structure or lattice geometry associated with the descriptor

requirements: Keep descriptor type and units explicit.
Record ANM, force-field normal-mode or FEM operator assumptions.
For a requested operator-level claim, measure mode directions, frequencies, couplings and relevant dissipation separately.
gaps: VibeGen amplitude target discards displacement directions.
Protein ANM and lattice FEM describe different physical systems and boundary conditions.
No shared calibrated full-dynamics operator is present in these profiles.
bridges.canGlue: A typed modal-descriptor registry and compatible mode-level questions.
bridges.temptingOverreach: Matching one modal descriptor recovers the full dynamical operator, cellular function or cross-system physical equivalence.
bridges.boundedClaim: A typed inventory of modal descriptors with their distinct information losses; no common dynamical operator is asserted.
bridges.strongerClaim: Matching one modal descriptor recovers the full dynamical operator, cellular function or cross-system physical equivalence.

bridges.label: Mechanism maps across scale
bridges.scientificClaim: A geometry-to-load-sharing-to-failure mechanism map can be compared while retaining the material-specific rupture and slip physics.

interfaceVariables.name: length_scale
interfaceVariables.meaning: Model-defined molecular or crystal length and confinement geometry

interfaceVariables.name: failure_mechanism
interfaceVariables.meaning: Slip, cooperative bond rupture or molecular rupture under stated loading

interfaceVariables.name: rate_and_boundary
interfaceVariables.meaning: Loading rate, hydration, confinement and reference-model assumptions

requirements: Keep each material’s dimensions and critical-length definitions separate.
Map the load-sharing mechanism rather than transferring raw fitted values.
Check rate sensitivity and relevant boundary conditions before numerical transfer.
gaps: Collagen main reference is hydrated, two-dimensional and cross-link-free.
Silk forces require rate correction; cited shear moduli are indirect comparisons.
bridges.canGlue: A bounded comparison of competing failure pathways and geometry-dependent load sharing.
bridges.temptingOverreach: One universal critical length or a whole-tissue toughness law follows from both simulations.
locators: SILK Figures2–5; Methods Application of boundary conditions
bridges.boundedClaim: A scoped comparison of two simulation-based geometry/failure mechanisms, retaining model-specific lengths.
bridges.strongerClaim: One universal critical length or a whole-tissue toughness law follows from both simulations.

interfaceVariables.name: retrieved_relation

interfaceVariables.name: traversal_rule

interfaceVariables.name: hypothesis_claim
interfaceVariables.meaning: Proposal linked to the supporting and limiting text

requirements: Retain evidence sources and contextual qualifications for each relation.
Resolve exact versus minimum shared-node traversal ambiguity.
Test causal or performance claims with independent material measurements or calculations.
gaps: Graph distance and incidence overlap do not establish mechanism or novelty.
Abstract-only novelty search cannot establish priority.
Generated dialogue and LLM judging do not validate material performance.

bridges.boundedClaim: A source-linked inventory of representations and proposal status; no causal gluing is asserted.
bridges.strongerClaim: A path connecting concepts identifies a causal interaction or demonstrates a novel working material.

bridges.label: Executed calculations and evidential closure
bridges.scientificClaim: Tool execution can support a bounded computational claim if model assumptions and numerical outputs are auditable.

interfaceVariables.name: calculation_spec
interfaceVariables.meaning: Geometry, electronic state or potential, boundary conditions and solver settings

interfaceVariables.name: execution_artifact
interfaceVariables.meaning: Actual script, inputs, logs and numerical outputs

interfaceVariables.name: checked_observable
interfaceVariables.meaning: Energy curve, barrier or toughness estimate with its numerical definition

requirements: Preserve actual inputs and outputs, not conversational success alone.
Audit physical-model adequacy separately from code execution.
Compare the target observable against a suitable numerical baseline and, for experimental claims, measurement.
gaps: MechGPT printed O2 code uses RKS/PBE/STO-3G; execution alone does not resolve adequacy.
AtomAgents uses human-authored LAMMPS scripts and task-specific support.
Neither computational success alone demonstrates physical validation.
bridges.temptingOverreach: An agent-run calculation is experimentally confirmed, autonomously general or physically correct merely because it completed.
bridges.boundedClaim: A comparison of computational execution evidence, keeping solver adequacy and experimental confirmation separate.
bridges.strongerClaim: An agent-run calculation is experimentally confirmed, autonomously general or physically correct merely because it completed.

requirements: Retrieve PROTOTYPE full methods before assigning its formal preservation rule or dynamics.
Specify which property is transferred and which experiment tests it.
Retain low confidence for abstract-only reported physical validation.

bridges.strongerClaim: A fabricated shape reproduces all nanoscale physics or inherits another paper’s validation.

interfaceVariables.name: output_type

Test reverse transfer, time dependence or generated materials separately if claimed.
